stat.health.description: How much punishment you can take before collapsing. Bandages are not a strategy, even if some crews seem convinced otherwise…
stat.morale.description: Helps you endure fear, defeats and extremely bad news. A proper banquet fixes many things. Not everything.
stat.strength.description: Used for close combat and developing Armament Haki. You will still lose to the Kung-Fu Dugongs…
stat.agility.description: Used to dodge, chase and escape situations that require functioning legs. Running on water is still reserved for absurdly trained people.
stat.observation.description: Helps you spot danger, read opponents and develop Observation Haki. Seeing the hit coming does not guarantee you can dodge it.
stat.intelligence.description: Used to understand, plan and solve problems that do not surrender after three punches. Yes, those exist.
stat.navigation.description: Used to read seas, currents and Grand Line's impossible routes. Without it, even a Log Pose mostly looks decorative.
stat.charisma.description: Helps persuade, recruit and impose your presence. Shouting that you will become Pirate King works surprisingly often, but not on everyone.
stat.luck.description: Matters when the plan is terrible but the universe has not decided to punish you yet. Does not replace a navigator or a brain.
npcStat.loyalty.description: Measures how attached a crewmate is and how willing they are to stay when everything goes wrong. Songs around a barrel help.
npcStat.calm.description: Measures the ability to keep a cool head under pressure. Useful when an Admiral decides your day was going too well.
ui.tooltip.world: Your current position and travel state. If the place name means nothing to you, confidently blame the navigator.
ui.tooltip.time: Your age and current career phase. On the Grand Line, getting older is already an achievement.
ui.tooltip.ship: Your ship, its type and condition. At 0 HP, it mostly becomes a very poor submarine.
ui.tooltip.crewRole: This crewmate's main job aboard the ship. Even pirates eventually discover the joys of an org chart.
ui.tooltip.crew: Current crewmates versus ship capacity. Go over it and someone inevitably ends up sleeping in a barrel.
ui.inventory.description: Two personal slots. Simple, fast, and difficult to turn into a junk drawer.
ui.inventory.personalItem.description: Personal item. Identical items remain stacked in the same slot.

ui.currency.berries.description: Your cash. Nothing forces you to spend it in the first bar you find.
ui.date.description: The OPFG calendar always starts in January 1507, two years after Luffy was born.
ui.monthEvents.description: The first pip fills after the first Event of the month and the second after the second. Both reset when the next month begins.
ui.ship.resistance.description: Current structural resistance of the ship.
ui.cargo.description: The first cell represents transport. The other seven are the maximum cargo slots.
ui.cargo.passenger.description: Temporary passenger: they also consume one cargo slot.
ui.cargo.item.description: Item transported in the ship cargo hold.

event.ch_generic_early_01_after_the_fall: {{npc_childhood_friend}} trips beside you and hits the ground hard. He sits there with his mouth open, not crying, as if he forgot how to breathe.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} grips your sleeve until his breathing returns.
Your shout turns a head. An adult arrives while {{npc_childhood_friend}} is still looking for you.
You stay within reach without touching him. {{npc_childhood_friend}} gets up by himself and sits against you.
Someone else helps {{npc_childhood_friend}}. When he leaves, he looks at the bench before looking toward you.
event.ch_generic_early_01_fallen_nest.te: {{npc_childhood_younger}} crouches over a fallen nest, already reaching toward the chicks. Two children behind her want to touch them before their mother returns.
event.ch_generic_early_01_fallen_nest.ch: Draw a circle around the nest
You push the curious children back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} stays crouched by the nest, relieved.
With leaves and a crate, you shield the nest from the footpath.
Show a feather to an adult
The adult understands when they see the feather. {{npc_childhood_younger}} keeps curious feet away until you return.
You back away to the wall. Two birds finally return above the nest, and {{npc_childhood_younger}} starts breathing again.
event.ch_generic_early_01_barking_dog.te: The tanner's dog lunges against its rope, barking. {{npc_childhood_younger}} freezes in the lane, too close to move forward and too proud to step back.
event.ch_generic_early_01_barking_dog.ch: You move between {{npc_childhood_younger}} and the dog. She does not let go of your arm until the next corner.
You back away together. {{npc_childhood_younger}} immediately claims she preferred this street anyway.
The owner pulls the dog back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} whispers a barely audible thank you.
You bolt. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is left behind, as angry as she is frightened.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} traps the ball under her foot. “It counted.” Another child swears it did not, and the game stops around you.
You jump in too fast. {{npc_childhood_rival}} and the other child only shout louder.
Nobody gives in. {{npc_childhood_rival}} tosses you the ball. “So what do we do?”
You make each of them repeat it. The fight is over one word, not cheating.
You propose one simple rule. {{npc_childhood_rival}} grins. “I’m keeping that one.”
You side with {{npc_childhood_rival}}. The other child cries foul, and she does not look away.
You leave the game. {{npc_childhood_rival}} takes the ball back without stopping you.
event.ch_generic_early_01_rules_of_game_: The other child points at {{npc_childhood_rival}}. “She has been cheating the whole time.” {{npc_childhood_rival}} looks at you, stung, before answering.
You replay the move slowly. The accusation looks weaker than it sounded.
You mix up two plays. {{npc_childhood_rival}} clenches her jaw and looks away.
You are no longer sure of the order. Nobody can settle the argument.
You remember the missing detail: {{npc_childhood_rival}} called her move before playing it.
You spot the mistake: they were using the same rule to mean different things.
You stop it before the insults start. {{npc_childhood_rival}} picks up the ball in silence.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} rereads the list from your parent. The written price is two Berrys too low, and there is nothing else in your pocket.
You stumble over the explanation. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} frowns and takes the list back.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not follow all of it, but he flips the price tag over to check.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} checks the tag: the price changed since yesterday.
You point out the date on the list. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} immediately sees where the mismatch came from.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} removes one item from the basket and hands the list back.
You leave with the list untouched. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} keeps the goods aside for when you return.
event.ch_family_social_01_market_errand_: Under the new tag, {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} finds the old price. “Your list isn’t wrong. But I still have to count what leaves the shop.”
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} copies the old price on the back. “Show them this at home.”
You return one item. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} ties up the rest of the parcel without comment.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} puts everything aside. “I won’t sell it before you get back.”
event.ch_family_social_01_friend_at_gate: {{npc_childhood_friend}} stops at your doorway. He looks at the set table, then at his dirty shoes, and cannot make himself step inside.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} steps in, slips on the rug, and knocks over a bowl. Every eye turns toward him.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} stays a few minutes, stiff in his chair, then invents an excuse to leave.
You make room away from the staring eyes. {{npc_childhood_friend}} eventually forgets about his shoes.
You turn the awkwardness into a joke. {{npc_childhood_friend}} walks in laughing and stops looking at the floor.
You grab your coat. {{npc_childhood_friend}} smiles before the door even closes.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} mutters, “At your place, I’m scared I’ll ruin something.” At least now you know.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} sets three pieces of wood on his bench. “If you want to learn here, show me how you would think this through first.”
You force a piece into the wrong place. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stops it before it snaps.
You get stuck. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} waits one more moment before putting the pieces away.
You find the right order. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} slides a real tool toward you, handle first.
You find a solution {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} did not show you. He resets the exercise to check it.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} agrees: one hour of tidying for one hour at the bench.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} puts the pieces away. “The offer stands if you change your mind.”
event.ch_family_social_01_household_ledg: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} sets his old ledger on the table. Your household owes three favors to the neighborhood, and someone has come to claim the first.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} half-closes the ledger. “Then I’ll come when someone needs you.”
You point at the entries you do not know. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} pulls out a second, much older notebook.
You push the ledger back. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not smile, but he does not reopen it either.
event.ch_family_social_01_ledger_s1_firs: A year later, {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} knocks with the ledger under his arm. A neighbor must clear her cellar before the rain, and your household is next on the page.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} crosses one line out of the ledger before you even leave.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} explains the work, then lets you decide with the facts in hand.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} closes the ledger. “All right. But the line stays.”
event.ch_family_social_01_ledger_s2_term: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} returns with three old entries circled in ink. “Your choice: carry this debt, verify it, or leave the ledger entirely.”
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} marks your choice with one hard line. The next requests will come to you.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stacks the old notebooks on the table. “Then we go through all of it.”
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} strikes your name out. For the first time, the page looks light.
event.ch_family_social_01_two_promises.t: Both your parents arrive at once: one promised you the docks, the other the neighborhood fair. Each was certain today belonged to them.
event.ch_family_social_01_two_promises.c: The first smiles. The other swallows their disappointment and says tomorrow will be their turn.
The second takes your hand. The first stays on the doorstep, annoyed despite the smile.
They look at each other, sigh, then change their plans. You will not have to choose after all.
They find you under the table a few minutes later. Both promises have now become an argument.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern.t: Your parent comes home after dark, shoulders soaked and eyes red with fatigue. The evening dishes are still waiting on the table.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern.c: Your parent stops at the nearly cleared table, then hugs you without a word.
You nearly fall asleep sitting up. Your parent carries you to bed when they arrive.
By morning, everything is put away. Your parent barely speaks over breakfast.
event.ch_family_social_01_late_lantern_r: This time, your parent comes home before dark. The lantern is out, dinner is warm, and they ask what you want to do with the evening.
You name the nights you waited. Your parent listens all the way through.
You leave the old evenings alone and keep this one for yourselves.
event.ch_family_social_01_parent_weak_da: Your parent drops their bag and sits on the floor before even taking off their shoes. They hand you the list of things they cannot finish today.
You take the first line. Your parent crosses out the rest and finally exhales.
Together, you keep only two things for today. The rest can wait.
You walk past the list without taking it. Your parent gets back up alone a few minutes later.
A few months later, your parent hands you another list, shorter this time. “I need a hand, not for you to carry everything.”
Your parent nods. This time, the refusal does not become an argument.
event.ch_generic_late_01_chain_of_favors: {{npc_childhood_friend}} helps you fix what you just broke, then refuses what you offer him. “Keep it. Help someone else when your turn comes.”
{{npc_childhood_friend}} finally accepts, mostly so you will stop insisting.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} holds out his fist. “Then we agree.”
You write the favor down. {{npc_childhood_friend}} rolls his eyes but lets you do it.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} gathers his tools. “Fine. We’ll see when your turn comes.”
event.ch_generic_late_01_shared_credit.t: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} praises your work in front of the whole shop, without naming {{npc_childhood_friend}} or the two others who carried half the boards. They heard it too.
event.ch_generic_late_01_shared_credit.c: You name each person. {{npc_childhood_friend}} straightens up, and {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} corrects his praise in front of everyone.
You correct nothing. {{npc_childhood_friend}} picks up another board without looking at you.
You point out the parts built together. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} understands before you finish the sentence.
event.ch_generic_late_01_younger_lookout: Three older teens want to climb the school roof and stick {{npc_childhood_younger}} on the corner as lookout. She says yes, but her voice shakes.
You pull her out of the plan. {{npc_childhood_younger}} complains in front of the others, then thanks you once you are alone.
You take the corner. {{npc_childhood_younger}} goes with the others but stays close enough to come back.
You turn the idea into a challenge on the ground. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is the first to agree.
You leave. When you look back, {{npc_childhood_younger}} is still alone on the corner.
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring.t: Three bigger children surround {{npc_childhood_younger}} behind the crates. She clenches her fists, but she is really looking for a way out.
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring.c: You stand beside {{npc_childhood_younger}}. The three others now have to decide whether they really want to continue.
You provoke them just enough to make them turn toward you. {{npc_childhood_younger}} takes one step back.
Your shout carries into the street. The three older kids are already looking for somewhere to run.
event.ch_combat_01_younger_in_the_ring_i: One of the bigger children shoves a crate across the exit. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is trapped between the wall and the rest of you.
You do not step back. {{npc_childhood_younger}} uses the hesitation to move closer to the exit.
You shift the crate just enough. {{npc_childhood_younger}} slips through the gap.
Hearing their own names breaks the pack mentality. Two of them step back.
The way out finally opens. {{npc_childhood_younger}} is outside, but the three others are still waiting to see what you do next.
You join {{npc_childhood_younger}} and leave together before anyone changes their mind.
You stay long enough for the threats to turn into muttering.
You do not give them the last provocation they were waiting for.
event.ch_combat_01_hill_sprint_rival.tex: {{npc_childhood_rival}} stamps twice at the starting line. “To the old fig tree. No shortcuts.” She takes off before the sentence is finished.
event.ch_combat_01_hill_sprint_rival.cho: Your foot rolls on a stone. {{npc_childhood_rival}} stops dead and comes back despite the race.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} gains three lengths. She looks back just enough to check you are still there.
You hold her pace into the bend. {{npc_childhood_rival}} finally stops smiling.
You find your rhythm and move ahead. {{npc_childhood_rival}} laughs out loud and accelerates.
You avoid the rocks on the shortcut. {{npc_childhood_rival}} catches you later, annoyed by the clever line.
You point out the slick ground. {{npc_childhood_rival}} grumbles, then agrees to walk back.
The path narrows between two walls. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is already dropping her center of gravity to take it without losing speed.
You keep your footing. {{npc_childhood_rival}} cannot shake you through the bend.
You copy her foot placement at the last moment. She notices at once.
You attack the bend. {{npc_childhood_rival}} answers without thinking and you come out side by side.
The fig tree appears at the end of the path. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is half a stride away, close enough to win or fall with you.
You almost touch the trunk together. {{npc_childhood_rival}} is already demanding a rematch.
You take the rocks. {{npc_childhood_rival}} follows instead of letting you risk them alone.
You slow by a fraction. {{npc_childhood_rival}} notices, bumps your shoulder, and laughs.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.title: {{npc_childhood_rival}}'s Line
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.text: {{npc_childhood_rival}} draws a line in the dust with her heel. “One round. No excuses.” The other children are already stepping back to watch.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed.choic: You step in directly. {{npc_childhood_rival}} plants her feet and waits with a grin.
You wait for her first move. {{npc_childhood_rival}} immediately realizes you will not rush in.
You set the rule. {{npc_childhood_rival}} raises an eyebrow, then offers her hand to seal it.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i1.te: {{npc_childhood_rival}} hooks your shoulder and tests your balance. Her feet move fast, but she gives you one second to answer.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i1.ch: {{npc_childhood_rival}} takes you down cleanly. The dust knocks the breath out of you for a second.
Neither of you finds the angle. {{npc_childhood_rival}} laughs through clenched teeth.
You shift her footing by half a step. Her grin disappears at once.
You reverse her grip and {{npc_childhood_rival}} hits the ground first. She bursts out laughing.
You give one step to understand the next. {{npc_childhood_rival}} immediately tries to surprise you.
You let her advance before pivoting. {{npc_childhood_rival}} nearly laughs at the worst possible moment.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i2.te: You both finish covered in dust. {{npc_childhood_rival}} offers her hand without asking who won.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_line_seed_i2.ch: {{npc_childhood_rival}} grips your hand. “Of course there’ll be a next time.”
You replay each move with your hands instead of your fists.
You leave without a verdict. {{npc_childhood_rival}} throws a handful of dust at your back.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s01_firs: Three months later, {{npc_childhood_rival}} is waiting in the same place. She has moved the line two steps and refuses to explain why.
{{npc_childhood_rival}} takes her stance before you finish answering.
You move the line again. {{npc_childhood_rival}} stares at you, then agrees without arguing.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s02_comp: {{npc_childhood_rival}} sits in the dust and points at your footprint. “There. That’s where I got you.” She waits for your answer.
You show her one mistake too. {{npc_childhood_rival}} repeats the move until she fixes it.
You smile without answering. {{npc_childhood_rival}} narrows her eyes; she will find it herself.
You split up with the same thought in mind: come back better.
event.ch_combat_01_rival_thread_s03_choo: {{npc_childhood_rival}} arrives with a question instead of a challenge. “Are we training to win, to improve, or to protect someone?”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} punches her palm. “Then we stop going easy on each other.”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} nods. “Then we count mistakes, not wins.”
{{npc_childhood_rival}} thinks for a second. “Then someone has to play the person we’re protecting.”
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape.title: {{npc_childhood_friend}} Mistaken for a Thief
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} crashes into a stall while running and the merchant shouts “thief.” Two vendors are already blocking the market exit before he can explain.
A hand catches your sleeve and throws you into a crate. {{npc_childhood_friend}} comes back instead of escaping alone.
The crowd closes the gap. {{npc_childhood_friend}} stays shoulder to shoulder so you are not split up.
You find the same rhythm and slip between two stalls before the gap closes.
You read the crowd one second ahead. {{npc_childhood_friend}} follows without asking why.
You open a gap for him. {{npc_childhood_friend}} hesitates, then runs and waits farther ahead.
You shout loudly enough for the first merchant to hear. His expression changes.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i1.text: A pile of baskets blocks the alley. Behind you, the vendors are gaining ground and {{npc_childhood_friend}} is already looking for another way through.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i1.choi: You spot a gap close to the ground. {{npc_childhood_friend}} slips through right behind you.
You drag one basket aside and open just enough room to get through.
You turn back into the main street, where everyone can hear your side.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i2.text: Two steps from the exit, a hand catches {{npc_childhood_friend}} by the sleeve. He turns instead of yanking away and tearing it.
event.ch_combat_01_market_escape_i2.choi: You peel the hand away without knocking anyone down. {{npc_childhood_friend}} moves again at once.
You call the first vendor by name. He finally gets close enough to hear you.
You step between them. {{npc_childhood_friend}} stays behind you instead of running off alone.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.title: {{npc_childhood_younger}} Behind the Door
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.text: {{npc_childhood_younger}} and two younger children shelter in a workshop while a group of angry teens pushes at the door. The back exit is still open.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.choice.b: You put your weight against the wood. {{npc_childhood_younger}} starts moving the two younger children out behind you.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold.choice.c: You clear the rear passage. {{npc_childhood_younger}} sends the first child toward the light.
Your shout carries through the walls. Outside, the blows against the door falter.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.title: The Latch Slips
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.text: The latch starts pulling out of the wood. {{npc_childhood_younger}} has almost moved the last child through the back.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i1.choic: You push the wood, not the people outside. The latch holds a few more seconds.
The crate wedges under the handle. {{npc_childhood_younger}} shouts that the rear way is clear.
You leave the door before it gives way and join {{npc_childhood_younger}} by the exit.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.title: Everyone Is Out
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.text: The last child is outside. {{npc_childhood_younger}} stays beside you while the older teens realize there is nobody left to trap here.
event.ch_combat_01_doorway_hold_i2.choic: You give them the street. {{npc_childhood_younger}} waits until they turn the corner before exhaling.
You point to the exit the younger children used. The insults suddenly sound much hollower.
You check the door while {{npc_childhood_younger}} counts the children outside. Nobody is missing.
event.ch_family_social_01_doorstep_guest: A soaked stranger knocks at your door. “Just until the storm passes.” No adult has come to see who is speaking yet.
You think you see a reassuring smile. When the man steps forward, you back away at once.
The rain hides his face and you cannot tell whether he is telling the truth.
He is genuinely shivering and keeps both hands visible, away from the handle.
You notice he is not looking inside, only at the roof above the doorway.
Let him stay under the awning
You show him where he can stay without opening the door further. He sits against the wall.
Close the door and call an adult
You close it. Outside, the man makes no attempt to push the door.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_badge.t: A man at the market notices the badge sewn to your bag. “Do you even know what that means?” You only know the story repeated at home.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_badge.c: You repeat what you were taught. The man listens without saying whether he believes it.
His answer sounds nothing like the one at home. You keep both versions in mind.
You turn the bag toward yourself. The man gets the message and moves on.
event.ch_family_social_01_family_reputat: What They Say About Your Family
Two adults ahead of you say your family name and laugh about a story you have never heard. One insists he “knows what your people are like.”
One of them recognizes you and goes quiet. The other realizes why too late.
They change the subject before giving the detail you wanted.
A name and a place come up twice. You know what to ask about at home.
You finally understand what they actually blame your family for, and what they made up.
You tell them your name. The laughter dies before you need to say anything else.
You leave them talking without giving them your face to remember.
event.ch_family_social_01_eviction_notic: A red notice is nailed to your door: three days to pay or get out. Your parent is not home yet, and the neighbors are starting to read it.
You mix up a date and think there is less time. Panic arrives before your parent does.
The formal wording does not help. Only one thing is clear: three days.
You find the amount, the date, and the owner’s name. At least nothing is hidden.
A recent payment is missing from the notice. You circle the line before your parent comes home.
A neighbor reads the notice with you and promises to stay until your parent returns.
You tear the notice down. The holes in the door remain, and so does the problem.
At the long table, a wealthy cousin looks at your clothes and asks loudly, “Do you always eat like that at home?” Several adults laugh without looking at you.
Your answer comes out too loud. The laughter stops, but now the whole table is watching you.
You answer without shaking, but your cousin keeps smiling.
You answer simply. Your cousin looks for a second joke and cannot find one.
Your answer makes the table laugh, this time at your cousin.
You ask the loudest adult a question. Within seconds, everyone is talking about something else.
You put down your napkin and leave before dessert. Nobody can pretend you heard nothing.
event.ch_generic_early_01_crowded_corner: {{npc_childhood_friend}} lets go of your sleeve between the stalls. One second later, three adults pass between you and you can no longer see his head.
Your voice cracks in the noise. {{npc_childhood_friend}} does not answer right away.
Nobody answers. You stay put despite wanting to run.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} answers from the other side of a stall. He was looking for you too.
You call his name at the right moment. {{npc_childhood_friend}} raises a hand above the crowd.
You get a little higher and spot {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s cap between two baskets.
The vendor climbs onto his crate and calls {{npc_childhood_friend}} with a voice that carries across the market.
event.ch_generic_early_01_storm_shutters: A shutter slams hard enough to knock down a frame. The adult beside you struggles with the window while loose objects roll across the floor.
A gust slams the wood near your head. You freeze halfway across the room.
The noise sends you back. The adult shouts for you to stay away from the window.
You hold the bottom of the shutter while the adult secures the latch.
You wait for the gap between gusts and help pull the shutter closed.
You pile bowls, papers, and tools where the wind cannot catch them.
You stay away from the window and hold the door shut when the adult asks.
event.ch_generic_early_01_small_delivery: {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} gives you a small parcel for the house at the end of the street. You know the door, but this is the first time you are going without an adult.
You mix up left and right at the first corner and return to {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}, annoyed with yourself.
You hesitate between two doors and finally ask for directions.
You recognize the right door handle and deliver the parcel without getting lost.
You find the simplest route and return before {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} finishes tidying the counter.
You make the trip together. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} does not tease you; the parcel gets there.
You hand the parcel back. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} takes it without pushing.
event.ch_generic_early_01_borrowed_broom: {{npc_childhood_rival}} grabs {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}’s broom like a sword. Her first swing kicks up a cloud of flour and sends three jars wobbling behind her.
You grab the other broom. {{npc_childhood_rival}} salutes you like a duelist in the middle of the white cloud.
You point at the jars. {{npc_childhood_rival}} puts the broom down just before {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} turns around.
You step back. {{npc_childhood_rival}} realizes too late that the third jar is still moving.
{{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} appears through the cloud just as a jar rolls toward the edge of the counter. {{npc_childhood_rival}} looks at you. “Run?”
You stop the jar with your fingertips. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} looks at the broom, then at {{npc_childhood_rival}}, then at you.
You slip in the flour and land in front of {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}}. {{npc_childhood_rival}} chokes back a laugh.
Two lids hit the floor, but the jar stays on the counter.
You catch the jar and one lid before they hit the floor.
You catch everything. {{npc_neighborhood_merchant}} stays silent long enough for {{npc_childhood_rival}} to stop smiling.
You put the broom down. {{npc_childhood_rival}} copies you, far too innocent to be convincing.
event.ch_generic_early_01_tidepool_glint: {{npc_childhood_younger}} points at a glint under the water between two rocks. Every wave covers it, and the water is already rising around your ankles.
You stare too long and a wave splashes both of you in the face.
The glint disappears under stirred-up sand. {{npc_childhood_younger}} swears it was still there.
You finally see it: a small copper medallion caught under a stone.
The glint moves on its own: a tiny crab is carrying a scrap of metal on its shell.
You reach into the water. {{npc_childhood_younger}} grabs your clothes when the next wave comes in.
You climb back to the dry rocks. {{npc_childhood_younger}} watches the glint until it disappears.
event.ch_generic_early_01_high_branch.te: {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s kite hangs from a branch above the path. He swears he can climb up himself, but his foot is already slipping on the bark.
event.ch_generic_early_01_high_branch.ch: The branch snaps under your foot. {{npc_childhood_friend}} reaches you on the ground before even looking at his kite.
You climb back down before reaching the branch. {{npc_childhood_friend}} does not make fun of you.
You free the kite and drop it straight into {{npc_childhood_friend}}’s hands.
You recover the kite without breaking a twig. {{npc_childhood_friend}} looks at you like it was a magic trick.
You nudge the branch from the ground. The kite falls between you.
You wait while keeping an eye on the tree. {{npc_childhood_friend}} refuses to leave without his kite.
Two small boats are heading for the same channel. The quay flag says “go,” but the current is pushing one straight toward the other.
You read the current backward and shout too early. A sailor corrects you at once.
You see the danger but cannot tell which boat should give way.
You identify the boat being carried by the current and shout to its pilot.
You read the drift before the pilots do. Your warning comes early enough for them to separate.
Both pilots look up. One second of hesitation is enough to break their collision course.
You run for someone who knows the signals. They understand the problem at a glance.
npc.childhood_friend.name: Childhood friend
npc.childhood_rival.name: Childhood rival
npc.childhood_younger.name: Younger neighbor
npc.neighborhood_merchant.name: Neighborhood merchant
ui.reputation.description: Measures how widely your name is known, without judging whether that reputation is good or bad.
event.ch_family_social_01_shared_bowl.te: Only three bites remain at the bottom of the bowl. The adult feeding you looks at the other plates before lowering the spoon again.
event.ch_family_social_01_shared_bowl.ch: Push the bowl to the middle
Pull the bowl back to you
Turn the spoon into a game
event.ch_generic_early_01_den_den_ring.t: A Den Den Mushi forgotten on a crate suddenly opens its eyes and starts ringing. Behind the door, the adults are talking too loudly to hear it.
event.ch_generic_early_01_den_den_ring.c: A voice says, “Hello?” You answer with very serious nonsense. Someone on the other end bursts out laughing.
The snail rings, and so do you. An adult finally enters, unsure which one of you to silence first.
Push the receiver to the door
You slide it forward inch by inch. A hand finally appears through the doorway and takes the call.
The ringing becomes a muffled grumble. Once freed, the Den Den Mushi stares at you with deep offense.
event.ch_generic_early_01_crab_in_basket: A tiny crab crawls out of a basket on the floor and grabs a bootlace. The person wearing the boot is asleep in their chair and hasn't noticed.
Push the basket back in front of it
You push the basket to its claws. The crab drops the lace and backs inside as if nothing happened.
The crab abandons the boot for your finger. Your yell wakes the entire room at once.
The sleeper wakes, looks at the living shoelace, then at you. Their laughter makes the crab let go.
You follow it without moving. It vanishes under a crate with four inches of shoelace between its claws.
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.title: The Big Red Smile
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.text: A painted mask falls from a travel bag and rolls to your feet. Its huge red smile stares at you while its owner keeps walking without noticing.
event.ch_generic_early_01_red_mask.choic: The owner doubles back and finds the mask upside down on your face. They laugh before taking it back.
You wave the mask like a flag. Someone calls the traveler back before they turn the corner.
Behind the smile, you find strings, repairs, and three older layers of paint.
The traveler comes back searching everywhere. Under the table, the red smile stays quietly with you.
event.ch_opening_household_orphan_01.cho: Clutch a crust to your chest
You keep the piece until the older children stop watching your hands.
Drag the basket under the awning
The basket scrapes over the stones. A baker sees you, hesitates, then closes the door without taking it back.
A hand comes back out with a still-warm bowl. You learn that here, making noise can sometimes be enough.
Let the older children choose first
They take the best and leave you the bottom of the basket. What you remember is who takes what.
event.ch_opening_household_orphan_01.tex: Behind a kitchen in {{birthplaceName}}, a basket of leftovers appears before dawn. Two older children are already watching the door, and nobody seems responsible for you.
event.ch_opening_household_marine_01.cho: Hold the helmet out to the soldier
{{npc_player_parent_1}} helps you lift it. The soldier gets his helmet back before the sergeant turns around.
Beat on it like a drum
Two recruits laugh while standing at attention. The sergeant does not, but {{npc_player_parent_1}} does.
An old corporal returns your salute with perfect seriousness. {{npc_player_parent_1}} immediately straightens your hand.
Push the helmet under the bench
The formation later breaks apart to search for the helmet. {{npc_player_parent_1}} figures out where it went before anyone else.
event.ch_opening_household_marine_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} carries you through the barracks yard. A training helmet falls from a bench as the recruits snap to attention.
event.ch_opening_household_pirate_01.cho: Pull the tricorn over your head
The tricorn drops over your nose. The table bursts out laughing and someone announces that the captain has arrived.
Three coins answer. {{npc_player_parent_1}} takes the purse back before its owner counts it a fourth time.
Point at the face on the poster
A pirate tells you the face's name, then the number underneath. Everyone seems to know the second one better.
Slide the purse under the table
The purse vanishes between your feet. {{npc_player_parent_1}} finds it first and gives you a much less amused look.
event.ch_opening_household_pirate_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} opens the door to three companions still covered in salt. A tricorn, a purse and a wanted poster land on the table before breakfast.
event.ch_opening_household_revolutionary: Pull the cloth over the paper
{{npc_player_parent_1}} sees what you did and immediately places a plate over it.
The paper disappears into a sleeve just before the door opens.
Everyone falls silent one second earlier. In this house, one second can be enough.
Crumple the paper in your fist
Ink smears between your fingers. The visitor goes pale; {{npc_player_parent_1}} swallows a sigh.
A visitor whispers with {{npc_player_parent_1}}, then slips a paper under the tablecloth. Someone knocks before he can put his coat back on.
event.ch_opening_household_bandit_01.cho: Three heads turn toward you. {{npc_player_parent_1}} covers your mouth, too late to stop the laughter.
Everything gets carried away except the sack you cling to. {{npc_player_parent_1}} comes back for it last.
You see figures leave the main road before the horses even appear.
Supplies roll across the floor at the worst possible moment. {{npc_player_parent_1}} has to choose between gathering them and leaving.
event.ch_opening_household_bandit_01.tex: {{npc_player_parent_1}} drops two dusty sacks by the door. Outside, a lookout whistles two notes and the whole camp suddenly starts moving.
event.ch_opening_household_prisoner_01.c: Follow the key with your eyes
The guard passes, returns, then passes again. Very quickly, you know when the key will appear.
Tap the bars when he passes
The guard speeds up without looking. {{npc_player_parent_1}} pulls you closer.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} says nothing, but stops taking their eyes off the hook.
The locks keep rattling, but you no longer have to look at them.
event.ch_opening_household_prisoner_01.t: {{npc_player_parent_1}} keeps you close behind a barred door. A key swings from the guard's hook every time he passes the cell.
event.ch_opening_household_slave_01.choi: {{npc_player_parent_1}} shares anyway, but keeps the smaller portion.
He always counts again before leaving the room. {{npc_player_parent_1}} waits for exactly that moment.
Hide a piece in your sleeve
The piece stays with you until evening. {{npc_player_parent_1}} understands what you did without asking.
Every head turns. {{npc_player_parent_1}} gathers the pieces before the overseer arrives.
event.ch_opening_household_slave_01.text: An overseer counts the bowls before serving. {{npc_player_parent_1}} receives one, keeps you close and waits for the man to turn away.
event.ch_opening_household_privileged_01: {{npc_player_parent_1}} moves your hand away. Even here, some doors do not open for you.
The guard bows before even understanding what you wanted.
A servant catches the cloth before it falls and waits for {{npc_player_parent_1}} to decide whether he may breathe.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} takes you back without comment. The servant immediately steps away.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} carries you through a corridor where servants and guards step aside without being asked. One gilded door remains closed.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_poor: Push a coin toward the list
{{npc_player_parent_1}} puts the coin back in the right pile and shows you the other two.
Cover a coin with your hand
{{npc_player_parent_1}} counts again, looks at you, then gently lifts your fingers.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} reads the purchases aloud as if you could already choose.
The coin disappears into a pocket. {{npc_player_parent_1}} thanks you very seriously.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} counts three coins before opening the shop. One is missing for everything written on the small list.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_mode: Point at the tool under the bench
{{npc_player_parent_1}} follows your finger and finds it immediately.
You copy the motions without fixing anything. {{npc_player_parent_1}} lets you finish anyway.
Drag the rag to the counter
The rag arrives covered in dust, but in the right place.
The shutter drops halfway. {{npc_player_parent_1}} has to open again, laughing.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} raises the workshop shutter before sunrise. The tools are in order, except for the one that is actually needed.
event.ch_opening_household_civilian_weal: Hand the key to the steward
The steward bows as if you had returned a treasure.
Try the key on a drawer
It is the wrong lock. {{npc_player_parent_1}} takes the key before the second attempt.
The steward freezes, then eventually lets you hear the whole keyring.
Slide the key under the rug
The search begins immediately. {{npc_player_parent_1}} looks at you long before the steward does.
{{npc_player_parent_1}} speaks with a steward carrying more keys than you can count. One slips from his belt onto the carpet.
Stop the drum with your foot
The drum stops against your shoe. The recruit recovers it without breaking stride.
You miss every other beat, but the last rank starts marching to your tempo.
Roll it back toward the recruits
The drum rolls between two pairs of boots and a hand catches it without stopping the column.
The column moves on. One recruit comes back alone a few seconds later, much less proud.
In {{birthplaceName}}, a drill blocks the street. A small marching drum escapes a recruit and rolls toward the gutter, right in front of you.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_outlaw_01.ch: Only an eye, a grin and part of the bounty remain. The number holds your attention most.
The man looks down the alley, then decides repasting the poster is less effort.
The face becomes almost whole again, but the bounty ends up across the forehead.
Fold the piece into your pocket
The paper is still sticky. Later, half the face is printed on your pocket.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_outlaw_01.te: In {{birthplaceName}}, a man pastes a wanted poster to a wall. Before the glue dries, someone tears half of it away and vanishes.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_port_01.choi: Stop a fruit with your foot
The fruit stops dead. A docker picks it up with one hand without letting go of his rope.
Stack the ones that stop near you
Your stack leans dangerously, but it keeps three pieces of fruit out of the water.
Chase the one rolling toward the water
You catch it at the edge of the quay with both hands. Behind you, someone claps exactly once.
The docker recounts the crate, sighs and goes back to work. The fruit stays with you.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_port_01.text: On a quay in {{birthplaceName}}, a rope snaps and a crate breaks open. Citrus fruit rolls between boots while the dockers hold the rest of the cargo.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_royal_01.cho: Wave the ribbon like a flag
A guard turns, hesitates between scolding you and laughing, then comes to retrieve it.
The ribbon remains behind the procession like a decoration nobody planned.
Offer it to the last guard
The guard takes it without breaking stride and gives you an almost invisible salute.
By the time the procession comes looking for it, the ribbon has already become your treasure.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_royal_01.tex: A small procession crosses {{birthplaceName}} under the guards' eyes. A long ribbon comes loose from a staff and falls behind them without anyone stopping.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_snow_01.choi: Hold the parcel over your head
The driver finally sees you and comes back swearing at the turn, not at you.
The tracks are easy to follow until the first crossroads, where they mix with all the others.
Something jingles inside. You learn nothing else, except that it is not bread.
The parcel almost disappears. The driver passes twice before finding it.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_snow_01.text: On a cold street in {{birthplaceName}}, a delivery sled turns too fast. A small tied parcel slips into the snow without the driver noticing.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_nature_01.ch: The piles match no recipe, but they are much easier to gather.
The smell makes you jerk backward. A voice from the shop says that was the correct reaction.
Stand up a bottle before it rolls
The bottle stops just before the gutter. Someone picks it up with very visible relief.
Chew the end of a leaf
It is horribly bitter. You spit it out before the shopkeeper can tell you to.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_nature_01.te: In {{birthplaceName}}, a basket of herbs and bottles tips over outside a shop. A sharp smell fills the street before anyone comes out.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_rural_01.cho: Offer it a handful of grass
The goat hesitates, drops the cloth and takes the grass. The owner cannot believe it.
Stand in the middle of the road
The goat goes around you without slowing, but loses enough time to be caught.
You do not catch it, but you learn exactly how far your legs can take you.
Grab the end of the cloth
The goat pulls from the other side. The cloth comes back in two pieces, one for each of you.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_rural_01.tex: Near a road in {{birthplaceName}}, a goat escapes with a market cloth in its mouth. Its owner comes after it, much slower.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_entertainmen: Push the coins back toward the hat
The musician keeps playing and bows to you in the middle of the chorus.
Passersby slow down to watch you. Two new coins land in the hat.
Spin a coin on the stone
The coin spins until the end of the verse. The musician finishes just in time to catch it.
Close your hand around one coin
The song ends. The musician counts the hat, shrugs once and starts playing again.
In a square in {{birthplaceName}}, a musician spins and knocks over his coin-filled hat. The song continues while the berrys roll away.
The roll knocks against the glass three times, then jams in the neck.
Hide it above the tide line
The sea will not take it back today. Nobody else knows it is there yet.
Carry it to the first houses
The bottle quickly passes from hand to hand. Everyone invents a different origin for it.
Put it back in the water
A wave immediately brings it back to your feet. The second attempt works better.
A wax-sealed bottle washes ashore near {{birthplaceName}}. No ship is visible on the horizon, but something rolled up taps against the glass.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_urban_01.cho: Roll the wheel back to the vendor
The wheel reaches his boot. He traps it without letting go of the cart.
You are not strong enough to right it, but strong enough to slow its fall.
You gather a small pile while the adults handle the cart.
The vendor eventually fixes the cart, then discovers his spare wheel is occupied.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_urban_01.tex: On a street in {{birthplaceName}}, a vendor cart loses a small wheel. The cart tilts, customers step back and the vendor tries to hold everything at once.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_coastal_01.c: Push it farther into the water
This time, the bottle gets past the small wave and actually begins to leave.
The bottle stops moving entirely. In a way, you have beaten the tide.
Watch every return of the wave
After a few passes, you know exactly how far the water will rise.
The next wave comes back empty. For the first time, the rhythm changes.
event.ch_opening_birthplace_coastal_01.t: The tide leaves an empty bottle on the edge of {{birthplaceName}}. Every small wave takes it, then brings it back to exactly the same place.
Push the boat back to him
{{npc_childhood_friend}} catches it, smiles, then immediately pushes it back. The game is decided without another word.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} inspects the pebble like treasure and immediately scratches a hold into the wood with his nail.
Hold the boat against your chest
{{npc_childhood_friend}}'s smile disappears. He does not take the boat back, but he does not go very far either.
The boat leans, spins and stays afloat. {{npc_childhood_friend}} crouches beside you to blow into its invisible sail.
event.ch_opening_friend_intro_01.title: The Wooden Boat
event.ch_opening_friend_intro_01.text: A child your age stops you with a boat carved from scrap wood. “{{npc_childhood_friend}},” he says, tapping his chest, then pushes the toy toward you.
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.choice: You find a trickle long enough for three voyages. On the fourth, the paper starts dissolving.
The sail holds better after three folds. {{npc_childhood_friend}} claims that was exactly his idea.
Let him choose the first launch
{{npc_childhood_friend}} chooses the fastest current and nearly loses the boat immediately.
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.title: One Sail for Two
event.ch_opening_friend_return_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} returns with the same boat and a crooked paper sail. “This one's ours,” he announces before looking for water.
You find a hiding place too small for an adult hand and just large enough for the coin.
Draw a map of the hiding place
The map mostly looks like three lines and a circle. You are still the only two who can read it.
Suggest trading it for a snack
The first vendor refuses the coin without touching it. {{npc_childhood_friend}} looks strangely relieved.
event.ch_opening_friend_cargo_01.title: The First Treasure
event.ch_opening_friend_cargo_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} returns with a bent coin no merchant would accept. To him, it is perfect: the boat now needs somewhere to hide its treasure.
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.choic: {{npc_childhood_friend}} takes it without smiling, but still sits beside you to inspect the hull.
He hesitates for a long time, then accepts the trade. The boat stays yours; the resentment, a little less.
Offer a race for the boat
{{npc_childhood_friend}} pulls his hand back and immediately draws a starting line with his foot.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} lowers his hand and leaves. He looks back once at the end of the street.
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.title: The Boat Reclaimed
event.ch_opening_friend_reclaim_01.text: {{npc_childhood_friend}} waits outside your home. He looks at the boat you kept, then at you. This time, he simply holds out his hand.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.f: Your boat jumps ahead, hits a leaf and capsizes just before the finish.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.b: You hold back enough water to launch both boats at once. The dam bursts behind them.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.choice.d: Draw a symbol on your sail
{{npc_childhood_friend}} immediately draws another. You decide that two crews have just been born.
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.title: The Gutter Race
event.ch_opening_friend_race_01.text: After the rain, {{npc_childhood_friend}} arrives with two small boats. The gutter in {{birthplaceName}} runs to the corner: to him, it is already a sea route.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.r: {{npc_childhood_rival}} starts half a second before everyone else. She calls it “being ready”; you call it something else.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.s: Spot a shortcut before the start
You spot an alley cutting the corner. {{npc_childhood_rival}} catches your look and smiles as if she just learned something about you.
{{npc_childhood_friend}} protests, then runs anyway. {{npc_childhood_rival}} points at you: “Next one is you.”
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.choice.c: {{npc_childhood_rival}} stares at you, picks up three stones and accepts immediately. The race has become something else.
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.title: The Line in the Dust
event.ch_opening_rival_intro_01.text: A girl called {{npc_childhood_rival}} draws a line in the dust of {{birthplaceName}}. “Race to the barrel. No excuses.” {{npc_childhood_friend}} is already taking a starting position.
originNarrative.location.military: Marine boots and barracks calls already set the rhythm of the streets.
originNarrative.location.outlaw: Merchants meet enough smugglers here to learn not to ask every question.
originNarrative.location.port: The quays mix cargo, dockworkers' shouts and crews that never stay long.
originNarrative.location.royal: Guards, clean walls and fine clothes remind everyone who rules.
originNarrative.location.snow: Cold wind presses salt and snow against the shutters.
originNarrative.location.nature: Forest, remedies and drying herbs begin almost at the doors of the houses.
originNarrative.location.rural: Houses spread out between dirt roads, fields and the smell of the sea.
originNarrative.location.entertainment: The streets live on music, crowds and travelers who change every week.
originNarrative.location.isolated: Here, every sail on the horizon becomes news for everyone.
originNarrative.location.urban: The alleys are full of shops, shouted orders and neighbors who know everything.
originNarrative.location.coastal: The sea is close enough to dictate schedules, trades and departures.
originNarrative.location.generic: Everyone eventually learns the same faces and the same rumors.
originNarrative.household.orphan: No stable home is waiting for you; you depend early on which doors open and which stay shut.
originNarrative.household.marine: {{familyReference}} lives by Marine orders and the timing of returning from duty.
originNarrative.household.pirate: {{familyReference}} lives among stained maps, passing crews and objects nobody explains.
originNarrative.household.revolutionary: {{familyReference}} knows names that are never spoken loudly and papers hidden before a door is opened.
originNarrative.household.bandit: {{familyReference}} hides supplies, watches the roads and rarely asks where a sack came from.
originNarrative.household.prisoner: {{familyReference}} shares with you a life ruled by locks, guards and imposed hours.
originNarrative.household.slave: {{familyReference}} teaches you early that meals, gestures and even time can belong to someone else.
originNarrative.household.celestial_drag: {{familyReference}} lives surrounded by servants and privileges almost nobody dares challenge.
originNarrative.household.royal_family: {{familyReference}} lives behind guards, court rules and a name others recognize before you do.
originNarrative.household.civilian_poor: {{familyReference}} counts berrys, keeps anything still useful and knows the price of a meal.
originNarrative.household.civilian_modes: {{familyReference}} works, pays what must be paid and knows the neighbors by name.
originNarrative.household.civilian_wealt: {{familyReference}} shields you from need, but not from expectations already attached to your name.
originNarrative.household.generic: {{familyReference}} becomes your first fixed point in the world.
originNarrative.race.fishman: Your Fish-Man body marks you out immediately in most Blue Sea streets.
originNarrative.race.mink: Your fur and Mink features draw looks anywhere your people are rare.
originNarrative.race.giant: Even as an infant, your size makes it impossible to mistake you for the other children.
originNarrative.race.longarm: Your long arms already force adults to adapt clothes, beds and gestures.
originNarrative.race.buccaneer: Your unusual build quickly draws looks your family learns to recognize.
